title: Image vs container
body: What is the difference between a Docker image and a container?

options.t: An image is a read-only template of layers; a container is a running (or stopped) instance of an image with its own writable layer

explanation: Many containers can run from one image. Container filesystem changes are lost when it is removed unless stored in volumes.

title: Layer caching in Dockerfiles
body: How should a .NET Dockerfile be ordered to maximise build cache reuse?

options.t: Copy the project files and run dotnet restore first, then copy the remaining source and build
Put RUN apt-get update in the last line

answer: Restore dependencies in a layer that only changes when project files change.
explanation: Docker reuses a layer when its instruction and inputs are unchanged, so dependency restores are skipped on code-only changes.

title: Multi-stage builds
body: What is the main benefit of a multi-stage Docker build?

options.t: The final image contains only runtime artefacts, not the SDK and build tools, making it smaller and safer

explanation: Build with the SDK image, then `COPY --from=build` into the aspnet runtime image (or a chiseled/distroless image).

title: Kubernetes Services
body: Which Kubernetes object provides a stable virtual IP and DNS name for a set of pods?
explanation: Pods are ephemeral with changing IPs; a Service selects pods by labels and load-balances to ready endpoints. Ingress or Gateway API exposes HTTP routes externally.

title: Readiness vs liveness probes
body: What happens when a pod's **readiness** probe fails?

options.t: The pod is removed from Service endpoints so it receives no traffic until it is ready again

explanation: Liveness failures restart the container; readiness failures only take it out of rotation. Startup probes protect slow-starting apps from premature liveness kills.

title: Undoing a pushed commit
body: A bad commit is already on the shared main branch. What is the safest way to undo it?

options.t: git revert <commit>, which creates a new commit that reverses the change

explanation: Revert preserves history for everyone. Reset/rebase/amend rewrite history and are fine only on unpublished local branches.

title: Rebase vs merge
body: What does `git rebase main` do on a feature branch?

options.t: Re-applies the feature branch's commits on top of main, rewriting them with new hashes for a linear history

answer: Replays commits onto the new base.
explanation: Rebase gives linear history but rewrites commits — avoid rebasing branches others have pulled.

title: Blue-green deployments
body: How does a blue-green deployment reduce release risk?

options.t: A new version runs alongside the current one; traffic switches once it is verified and can switch back instantly
By updating servers one file at a time

answer: Two environments with an instant traffic switch.
explanation: Canary releases shift a small percentage of traffic first. Database migrations must be backward compatible (expand/contract) for either strategy.
